steps.content: Two days later, the sandstorm is still raging.
Hiding in a flimsy wooden building of an oasis shelter is completely different from hiding in a sturdy sand ship. Even in the cellar, one can feel the full fury of the storm above.
The dilapidated cellar door suddenly opens from the outside, and wind mixed with white sand gushes in. A tightly bundled figure jumps down, closing the wooden door behind him.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I'm back!
The boy holds a supply box high above his head. The task force members greet him with warm smiles. They have long grown accustomed to his ways.
Though this young, self-proclaimed geologist is socially awkward and lacks common sense, he is one to be trusted in times of crisis.
What's more, in the few days spent with the task force, the boy's common sense is also rapidly developing.
In the past few days, many things in the fortress were blown away by the sudden sandstorm before they could be packed away.
The reserves in the cellar were low, so Kawa-kawa constantly went up to the surface to find supplies, saving everyone from starvation.
He refused to let anyone help him, citing the risk of getting lost in the sandstorm for those unfamiliar with the desert.
Everyone can only shrug and let him show off his prowess.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Just as the data predicted, the sandstorm has already started to shrink. It will recede almost completely by tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I checked all the beacons. They're all tightly fastened to the fortress wall. Speaking of which, I really have to thank them.
Kawa-kawa glances at the desert bandits in the cellar corner, who have their hands tied behind their backs.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: They placed so many beacons in the oasis, and the center of this sandstorm just happens to be here. The data collected from this storm is priceless!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did yesterday's signal go out?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Don't worry! As long as no one from the sand ship took down the beacon I set up, the information must have reached the captain.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Oh, right! I found some food to share with you all!
Everyone's eyes lit up as soon as they heard the word "food." They've been eating nothing but compressed food for the past two days.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Hehe... I found some good stuff.
Kawa-kawa puts down the supply box, squats down and starts rummaging through his backpack.
He fishes out a few scrawny lizards with one hand, and some scorpions with broken tails with the other.
Some task force members almost shriek out and faint.
You recall that during the first WhiteSands operation, Kawa-kawa mentioned eating grilled scorpions, which according to him, taste like chicken.
You realize now that it wasn't a joke.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Of course! This is a rare delicacy of WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Although there's not much meat on them, they're very delicious when grilled and seasoned!

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Animals and insects are much more perceptive than humans.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: During a sandstorm, you can easily find them hiding together, especially in the corners of buildings.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I found these in the dock.
With that, he skillfully lights a fire before everyone's gawking eyes.
He slices open the lizards and scorpions with a small knife and sprinkles them with fine salt. He then skewers them with dead branches and holds them over the fire.
Though unsettling to look at, the delicious aroma of grilled meat soon wafts throughout the cellar.
Like a gourmet chef, Kawa-kawa fans the flames with his hat to control the heat.
He cooks like this for around five minutes.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: It's ready! Who wants to take the first bite?
One must admit that the grilled lizard skewers look much more appealing now.
The lizards' fat has turned golden brown from the open fire, while the lean meat has become like jerky.
Even so, no one dares to take a skewer from Kawa-kawa.
You, however, disregard the uneasy atmosphere by the fire. You not only take a lizard skewer, but a scorpion skewer as well.
You take a bite. Kawa-kawa has grilled them with the perfect amount of heat. The skin is crispy, while the meat inside is tender and juicy.
The scorpions, on the other hand, are crispy and succulent all over, especially when seasoned with fine salt. You can't help but give a big thumbs up in the direction of the desert bandits.
For the past two days, everyone had only compressed biscuits to feed on, which were as bland as a mouthful of sand.
After hearing your praise, the task force members can't help but salivate.
Hecate makes the first move. Then, one after another, everyone scrambles to grab the skewers by the fire.
Soon, the task force members can't stop praising the food. The boy smiles happily.
Ten hours later, Oasis fortress tower
The sandstorm subsides, just as Kawa-kawa has predicted.

After three days of tense nerves, the task force is finally able to get a good night's sleep. Kawa-kawa, however, says he's not tired, and that he'll take the final night shift for the task force. He wants to keep an eye on the beacon data in case another sandstorm comes.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Chief, why are you still awake?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Someone needs to watch the desert bandits in the cellar. But don't worry, I asked Hecate to go.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I'm used to it. For many years, when I was surveying in WhiteSands, I could only do research when the temperature dropped at night.
The boy sits cross-legged atop the tower as he talks, with a thick notebook and map on his lap, and a fire next to him to keep him warm.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you working on this time?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I'm pulling the data on the previous sandstorms from the beacon network and putting them into the model.
You can see the fatigue on the boy's face, yet something is spurring him to keep working on the data.
You sit down next to him by the fire. You take a portable terminal out of your pocket and hand it to the boy.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: What's this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: An application for a transfer order I just wrote. When we get back, I'll start the formal approval process.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: You're going to transfer me to... the task force?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your Sinner power is very special and can protect others well. Coupled with your performance in battle, I don't think there should be any obstacles in getting the approval.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Also, don't you want to return to WhiteSands to continue your surveying work? By joining the task force, I can regularly arrange for you to go to WhiteSands on missions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After this transfer order is approved, you can use all the supplies in the WhiteSands base station.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Think of it as a fringe benefit. But you have to promise me one thing.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: A-and what is that?

options: You have to promise not to escape.

choices.text: You have to promise not to escape.

steps.content: Kawa-kawa takes a deep breath, then hugs the terminal in his arms, trying his best to stop shaking with excitement.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Thank you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No need to thank me. Remember what I said? I'm just trying to the best of my ability to repay you for the kindness you've given to this world.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your contributions to WhiteSands' routes shouldn't just be respected by us, but by everyone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If it weren't for the beacons you set up, the sand ship would've struggled to navigate WhiteSands. The task force would've also had a hard time reaching the oasis.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: ...Thank you, you're very kind too. My dad would've been proud to hear this.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Yes, my dad. My grandpa, also. Three generations of my family have been surveying and mapping WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: They would've all been thrilled to hear this.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: After all, this is the first praise I've ever gotten for our work.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That notebook in your backpack, and that forecasting model... Did your dad leave you those?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Yeah, those are my dad's valuable research materials. But... I haven't seen him for almost a decade.
The temperature of WhiteSands at night is totally opposite to that of daytime. Kawa-kawa tightens his scarf and adds some more wood to the fire.
The firelight illuminates the boy's face, but you can't tell what he's thinking.
You wait for the boy to continue on his own, asking no questions.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I never met my grandpa, and my mom died giving birth to me. As for my dad... He only returns to the shelter once in a while. Sometimes, I wouldn't see him for a whole month...
The boy smiles sadly.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Growing up, I was quite unpopular in the shelter. You know what they called me? The "idiot's son." That father of mine was a lot of trouble.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Every time he came back to the shelter, he told me he was working on a great cause.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But he was so sly, he never told anyone else about what he was doing. He never let the townspeople know that he was mapping WhiteSands, or that he dreamed of finding safe passages and harbors there.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I told him I wanted him to just stay in the town and be like everyone else's fathers. I wanted him to take my hand and go to the grocery store at dusk.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: This continued until I was six. I haven't seen him since.

options: Did anyone else see him since?

choices.text: Did anyone else see him since?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: No one has seen him since. Every day, I sat on top of the crate at the entrance of the town, waiting for him as always. It was the path he'd take to come home.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Sometimes I thought that maybe I'd feel better if he really died in an accident.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But you know what? When I was eight, I got a package from him.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: He didn't put any letters in the package, but I knew he was the one who sent them. Only he would send those fancy research materials to such a little border town.

options: And they're the manuscripts you have on hand?

choices.text: And they're the manuscripts you have on hand?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: That's right.
The boy takes out the manuscripts from his luggage. The dozens of handwritten pages have yellowed from the years, but there are no signs of damage. They have been perfectly preserved by Kawa-kawa.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I thought about it for a long time. Why did he send me these materials? The townspeople told me not to think about such useless things. They laughed at me and said that if I did, I'd become an idiot just like him.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But I just couldn't help thinking about my dad's "great cause."
You couldn't figure it out, so you tried to chase after him, right?
The boy freezes in surprise.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: ...How did you know?

options: That's what they call souls in sync.

choices.text: That's what they call souls in sync.

steps.content: The boy's actions have always been upright. Coupled with his current situation, it wasn't hard to guess.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Amazing! Just like Stargazer!

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: You're right. And it wasn't hard to follow my dad's trail. There was a beacon set up only a kilometer away from the shelter.
So you followed the beacons, one by one, into WhiteSands.
And on that journey, you awakened your Sinner power.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: That's right. Looking back at it now, it was actually extremely risky. I went into WhiteSands with just enough food and water for less than a week.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Then, unsurprisingly, a few kilometers into WhiteSands, I encountered a massive sandstorm.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: You should know what it's like to see a beacon shining brightly in a sandstorm when you can be torn to shreds anytime.
You've faced the full horror of sandstorms, so you can easily visualize the scene.
You remember the despair, fear and powerlessness you felt when Stargazer rescued you last time. Those feelings almost suffocated you, and the boy was probably in an even worse situation at the time.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I could only follow the beacons, one after another, on and on.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I didn't know how long I had been walking. I didn't know which direction I was heading. That was, until I reached a harbor at the very last beacon.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I knew I was saved.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: At that moment, I understood firsthand what my dad's "great cause" meant. I realized what this cause could bring to others.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I realized that I should devote my life to this cause, for there is nothing greater than saving the lives of others.
The wind around you dies down completely. All you can hear is the crackling firewood by you and the boy.
I checked some information on your grandpa. He was a well-known geologist who devoted his life to forecasting sandstorms. And your dad was your grandpa's best student.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: The theoretical model for forecasting sandstorms was created by my grandpa. But the model requires massive amounts of dynamic data to function.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: And in WhiteSands... Whether it's exploring or setting up a beacon network, the work is hard and thankless.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I heard that no one supported my grandpa's project, so he and my dad had to finish the model themselves.
You've reviewed the files and inventions of Kawa-kawa's grandpa. The forecasting model is actually very accurate, but it threatened the vested interest groups of DisCity.
If safe transport routes are established in WhiteSands, Nirvana's status will be severely hit. In the worst case scenario, Hypercube prices may crash...
So the authorities promised him the most cutting-edge research equipment in exchange for staying in WhiteSands forever.
This is the reason why Kawa-kawa's family had been living in WhiteSands for generations. To keep the precious research resources, Kawa-kawa's grandpa had no choice but to accept such a deal.
But obviously, the boy is not yet ready to touch upon such realistic issues.

options: The awakening of every Sinner's power is related to the Black Rings.

choices.text: The awakening of every Sinner's power is related to the Black Rings.

steps.content: Many of them call their powers a curse, and have caused much misfortune wherever they go.
But Kawa-kawa, you're different. You've done things that many others haven't been able to. You've made good use of your power, bringing happiness to others with your "curse." You're very lucky.
Of course, all those years of surveying, mapping, and setting up beacons in WhiteSands isn't something that can be easily surmised by luck.
The boy has perseverance unimaginable to most, but at the root of the matter is the unshakable faith he inherited from his forefathers.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Yes... I was awakened during that sandstorm. My mind has changed since then.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I no longer thought of my dad as the "idiot" that others sneer at. As for myself, I feel like I should do even better than my dad after gaining this power. Only...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I followed all those beacons in WhiteSands, searching all the way. In my seven years of searching, I finished every geology book and figured out every piece of data and model in those manuscripts...

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I thought that maybe my dad was testing me, and that he'd come back to me if I completed the test.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Or maybe he just had too much work, and that he'd come back early to meet me if I helped him complete part of it.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But I was wrong.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Half a year ago, I walked across half of WhiteSands and found my dad's last beacon. There ought to have been another beacon a kilometer away, but I didn't see it.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: I looked in every direction but found nothing. I was finally convinced that it was the last beacon my father had set up.

options: You didn't find any other information?

choices.text: You didn't find any other information?

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: No.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: The beacon stood alone amid the dunes. I stayed by that beacon for a week, thinking that maybe my dad left for a run, and that I'll bump into him on his way back.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: But it's just like when I was six years old, I sat at the entrance of the town, waiting for him. In the end...
You gently touch his head.
...That day will come.
Maybe your dad will follow your beacons to find you.

steps.speaker: Kawa-kawa
steps.content: Sob...
The knot in his heart that had stayed there for seven years finally unravels with the wind.
Your dad and grandpa would be proud of you.
The data terminal in the boy's hand falls to the ground. The data finishes uploading to the beacon network. After a five-second countdown, the beacon network of the oasis resumes functioning.
The beacons around you light up one by one. From the high tower, they look like blue fireflies illuminating the dark desert.
They link all the way to the night sky, merging with the stars.
It's as if a second Milky Way has spread out across WhiteSands.
